picks.intervention_label: Sequential conditioning into a second allograft (CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida then RIC, NCT04375631; DEC-FLAG-Ida then TBI/RIC, NCT06928662)
picks.rationale: The largest true-CR figure in this file belongs to a procedure rather than a drug: 88% (66/75) with FLAMSA sequential conditioning, and ASAP's randomised answer was day-56 CR of 83% in patients given no induction at all against 79% in those induced. Upside if it lands: the remission is manufactured by conditioning plus a second graft's graft-versus-leukaemia, neither of which cares that her clone is quiescent, p53-broken or BAX-mutant, and on the TBI platform the thigh sarcoma sits in the field instead of waiting on a marrow answer. The evidence for her specifically is thin in both directions, since FLAMSA was mostly first transplants two decades before venetoclax and ASAP excluded prior allograft, but NCT04375631 defines refractoriness as failure of two venetoclax cycles or one high-dose cytarabine course, which is her, and offers a cladribine debulk instead of the FLAG-Ida she already failed. I would take an 88% with a flawed denominator over a well-matched 13% that tells her she probably will not reach CR at all.
primary_concerns: Second allograft with roughly 85% marrow blasts is the highest-mortality move on the board, and her organ function is undocumented; if the labs come back poor this pick dies rather than gets softened
NCT06928662 debulks with DEC-FLAG-Ida, which re-exposes her to the regimen she just failed; the cladribine arm of NCT04375631 is the version of this platform I actually want
Both protocols read out transplant failure and progression, not CR, so nothing published will tell the team the remission rate before she signs
Donor work-up, screening and a second-graft slot take time, and her peripheral blasts moved 58 to 82 percent inside a few weeks
FLAMSA's 88% predates venetoclax-era salvage; nobody has generated that number in a patient who has already rejected an allograft's worth of GvL pressure

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
picks.rationale: No published results in refractory AML is a real hole and I am picking it anyway, because the family figure is a true CR of 58% (66/118) rather than a composite, the only head-to-head in the dossier puts cladribine over MEC at 37.9% against 23.8% true CR (p=0.048), and cladribine lifts ara-CTP accumulation in circulating blasts by about 40%, which is exactly the arm of the mechanism an 82% peripheral blast count needs. Fractionated gemtuzumab adds the one extramedullary datum anywhere in this file: two children whose CD33-positive lesions shrank on serial PET/CT, worthless as an estimate and worth something as proof a systemic CD33 agent reaches tissue. Eligibility is the rare part, since NCT04050280 takes post-allo relapse from 60 days out with no blast or WBC cap and its exclusion names cladribine and gemtuzumab rather than fludarabine. What could sink it: the 58% came from a pre-venetoclax cohort in which WBC above 10 g/L predicted treatment failure, and single-agent CD33 targeting bought only 26% CR in first relapse.
primary_concerns: Her own protocol has zero efficacy data; the only CLAG-GO publication is frontline core-binding-factor AML, a different disease
Gemtuzumab's contribution rests on qualitative CD33 flow with no antigen density, and veno-occlusive risk in someone who has already been through a transplant is not a footnote
The 58% carries no post-allo subgroup and no venetoclax-exposed patients, so the read-across is mine, not the paper's
Response assessment on this protocol is marrow-based; a CR could be declared with the thigh lesion still there

picks.intervention_label: HAM plus venetoclax (high-dose cytarabine, mitoxantrone, venetoclax), RELAX / NCT04330820
picks.rationale: CRc 75% (41/55) is the highest remission number among deliverable chemotherapy backbones, and 19 of the 55 had a prior allograft, a combination no other salvage series here matches. It is a composite with no CR-only split, and her second-salvage venetoclax-refractory state fell outside enrolment, so I am quoting a figure from a population that would have turned her away. The reason I still want it: dynamic BH3 profiling re-primes venetoclax-resistant myeloblasts, and the BAX mutants selected during BCL-2 antagonist exposure keep variable rather than absent chemotherapy sensitivity, so failing venetoclax alongside FLAG-IDA does not settle what venetoclax does on top of high-dose cytarabine and mitoxantrone. If the trial cannot take her, the regimen can be built from marketed drugs off protocol, which is the practical reason it sits at rank 3 rather than lower.
primary_concerns: Re-dosing venetoclax in a patient whose disease grew through it is the weakest link, and the BH3 re-priming argument is bench work, not a response rate
Composite CRc with no CR split means the honest CR estimate behind that 75% could be anywhere
Trial recruitment status reads unknown; off-protocol assembly means no trial support and no protocol-defined response assessment
Prior anthracycline exposure plus undocumented cardiac function before mitoxantrone
53% grade 3 or worse rate in a cohort healthier than she is

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-M off protocol (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, mitoxantrone, G-CSF)
picks.rationale: If protocol screening for NCT04050280 or a transplant slot eats weeks she does not have, CLAG-M off protocol is the same cladribine backbone and it can start immediately, at a true CR of 58% (66/118) after one or two courses. The honest reading of that 58%: no post-allo subgroup, venetoclax did not exist when it was generated, and poor karyotype was the single variable that cut disease-free survival. Set against the numbers that genuinely describe her position, 13% true CR at second salvage across 594 patients and a 23% response rate after venetoclax salvage failure that pools CR with MLFS, a high-intensity cladribine backbone has the fattest right tail of anything she can start on Monday. Every one of those assessments is marrow-only, so I would irradiate the thigh concurrently rather than find out afterwards that the sarcoma sat through the whole thing.
primary_concerns: WBC above 10 g/L predicted treatment failure in the source cohort and she is far past it
Cytarabine-based killing depends on cell-cycle position, and the endosteal LSC that reseed her marrow survive it; a morphologic CR from this backbone may be shallow
Off protocol means no trial infrastructure, and 7% early death in a cohort that had not just failed FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax after an allograft
Prior anthracycline load plus undocumented cardiac and hepatic function

notes: Two things I want on the record. First, the best mechanism fit in this dossier is lintuzumab-Ac225 after CLAG-M: alpha emission kills independently of cell-cycle position and p53, and it re-sensitised venetoclax-resistant AML in vivo (pmid:33347715), with composite CR/CRi of 50% in the TP53-mutated and 38.5% in the prior-venetoclax subgroups. I have not ranked it because the trial is completed and NCT06802523 is suspended, and deliverability is a hard constraint. Somebody should still make the expanded-access call to the sponsor before this board closes, because if the answer is yes my ranking changes. Second, I will argue against CPX-351 plus venetoclax in round 2 despite its population match: true CR was 15%, the within-protocol split puts her in the 26% arm rather than the 70% one, and its tissue-to-plasma ratios run below 1 where free drug runs above 1, which is the wrong direction for a lesion in her thigh.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
picks.rationale: The cladribine backbone carries the best true-CR evidence among the regimens she can actually receive: 58% CR in 118 poor-risk refractory and relapsed patients, and 37.9% versus 23.8% for CLAG over MEC in the one head-to-head comparison in this file (p=0.048). NCT04050280 is the only open protocol that takes her at 85% blasts more than 60 days out from her graft, and using fractionated gemtuzumab instead of mitoxantrone avoids adding anthracycline to a cumulative dose nobody has documented, while keeping a drug that produced no grade 3-4 liver toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease in MyloFrance-1, including the seven patients transplanted afterwards. On protocol she also gets the baseline organ-function screen this case has never had. My support is conditional on that screen: creatinine clearance, transaminases, bilirubin and cardiac function documented before day 1, and the gemtuzumab component re-adjudicated if hepatic labs are abnormal at baseline, because she is a candidate for a second graft and that is where fractionated dosing earns its safety record or loses it.
primary_concerns: The protocol has zero published results in refractory AML. I am extrapolating from the components, and a component-wise safety argument is weaker than a regimen-level one.
The 58% CR figure comes from a series that closed before venetoclax existed and reports no post-allogeneic-HCT subgroup at all. Her two hardest axes are simply absent from it.
Wierzbowska named WBC above 10 g/L and age over 34 as predictors of failure. She trips both, and Giles puts second-salvage CR at 13% of 594 with 0% in the highest-risk group.
Gemtuzumab plus a second allograft is the veno-occlusive disease scenario. MyloFrance-1 saw none in seven transplanted patients, which is reassurance from a denominator of seven, not proof.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-M (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, mitoxantrone, G-CSF) off protocol
picks.rationale: If the trial slot does not open inside the few weeks her peripheral count trajectory allows, the same backbone off protocol is the fallback, and it is the one option here whose toxicity is fully tabulated rather than inferred: severe infection 45%, 8 early deaths in 118 (7%), and in the patients who reached CR, neutrophils under 0.5 g/L for a median 24 days and platelets under 20 g/L for 23 days. That is a long aplasia in a marrow that has already been through FLAG-IDA and a graft, but every event in it has a standard management algorithm behind it. I rank it second rather than first because off protocol nobody is obliged to document her organ function first, and mitoxantrone goes into a patient with no recorded ejection fraction and an unknown cumulative anthracycline dose from prior idarubicin. The threshold is simple: no mitoxantrone without an echocardiogram or MUGA and a creatinine clearance on file.
primary_concerns: Anthracycline-class exposure on top of undocumented prior idarubicin, in a patient with no cardiac assessment anywhere in the record.

Zhong's blast-burden gradient is the number that worries me most about any high-dose cytarabine backbone here: response odds more than doubled at marrow blasts at or below 20% and peripheral blasts at or below 30%, and she is at roughly 85% and 82%.
A median 24 days of neutropenia after a prior transplant is where the published early-mortality figure of 7% is likely to understate her, since no post-allo patients were in that series.
Five of the eight early deaths were febrile neutropenia and sepsis. Manageable is not the same as survivable at her marrow reserve.

picks.intervention_label: Hypomethylating agent plus venetoclax for post-allograft relapse
picks.rationale: This is the branch I want available in writing before anyone books an intensive induction, because it is where she goes if the organ-function screen comes back marginal, and it is also the closest published population to hers: 83 patients relapsing after allograft, 55% with prior venetoclax and 28% of those already failed on a venetoclax regimen, composite CR/CRi 48% and explicitly not a true-CR figure. What buys it a place on a CR-maximising list is the mortality column: 3 deaths within 30 days of 83 (3.6%), against 7% early death for CLAG-M and 21% by day 60 for CPX-351 plus venetoclax. Cytopenias were near universal, grade 3-4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia both 99%, but febrile neutropenia only 24%, so the marrow cost is real and the infection cost is the lowest of anything on this list. Against it, honestly: 85% marrow blasts is a great deal of disease for a regimen that works on kinetics, and she has already progressed through venetoclax, where Zucenka's post-venetoclax salvage cohort managed 23% ORR in 22 patients with 6 of 28 too unwell to treat at all.
primary_concerns: 48% is CR plus CRi pooled. The true-CR component is not published, so this number cannot be lined up against Wierzbowska's 58% without misleading someone.
Retrospective, single centre, and the venetoclax-failure subgroup within it is 28% of 55%, which is roughly 13 patients.
Time to response. She rose from 58% to 82% peripheral blasts across late June, and an HMA-paced regimen may not move fast enough regardless of its safety profile.

Nothing in the source assessed the thigh sarcoma or any extramedullary site, and 56% of paired myeloid-sarcoma and marrow samples carry discordant mutation profiles, so a marrow answer here would not be a whole-patient answer.

picks.intervention_label: CPX-351 (liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine) plus venetoclax, NCT03629171
picks.rationale: Best population match in the dossier and I still put it fourth, because the true CR is 15% of 33 and the 39% that will get quoted is the composite. The subgroups that make it look matched to her are small: CRc 50% in the prior-transplant patients, 32% in the prior-venetoclax patients, 26% in second salvage or TP53-mutated, all on denominators in the single digits to low teens. The price is documented and steep, which I will take over undocumented any day, but it is still grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 76%, bacteraemia 64%, pneumonia 27%, six grade 5 events, 9% dead by day 30 and 21% by day 60. Asking a patient with no baseline organ function on record to accept a one-in-five chance of dying inside 60 days for a 15% chance of the endpoint she wants is a trade I would only put to her with the labs in hand, and I would want the venetoclax re-exposure argued on its own merits given she progressed through it weeks ago.
primary_concerns: 21% mortality at 60 days is the highest documented early-death figure among the deliverable options here, and it comes from a cohort with organ function screened at entry, which she has not had.

Re-exposure to venetoclax in a patient refractory to FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax. Acquired BAX loss and reduced apoptotic priming after venetoclax failure are the mechanistic reason to expect less, not more.
Daunorubicin, even encapsulated, is more anthracycline into an unmeasured cardiac reserve.

RELAX (HAM plus venetoclax, composite CRc 75%, 35% prior allo-HCT) will be raised as the better venetoclax-era intensive option, and it required adequate hepatic and renal function at entry. Her eligibility for that comparison is unestablished in both directions.

picks.intervention_label: Sequential FLAMSA-type conditioning into a second allograft (US analogue DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC, NCT06928662)
picks.rationale: I keep this on the list because ASAP is the only randomised test of whether buying a remission before transplant is worth what it costs, and day-56 CR came out 83% with watchful waiting against 79% with induction, a difference of 3.4% (95% CI -5.8 to 12.6), with 40 points less grade 3+ non-haematological toxicity and 27 fewer hospital days in the arm that skipped induction. The honest reading is that non-inferiority failed at the pre-specified 2.5% level (p=0.036) and neither arm separated, and prior allo-HCT was an exclusion, so it does not transfer to her. FLAMSA's 88% CR in 75 patients is a genuine true-CR figure rather than a composite, but it comes from mostly first transplants in the pre-venetoclax era, and NCT06928662 has no remission data of its own. It sits last on a CR question and not lower because the remission-producing toxicity here is second-graft non-relapse mortality, which is the one adverse event on this page with no rescue algorithm behind it.
primary_concerns: Non-relapse mortality after a second allograft in active refractory disease is the load-bearing risk, and neither the FLAMSA series nor NCT06928662 gives me a figure for it in a post-allo population.
The 88% CR predates venetoclax-era salvage and describes patients who had not already failed an intensive regimen plus venetoclax.
SIERRA showed radioimmunoconditioning can carry active disease to a durable CR at 17.1% versus 0%, but it excluded prior HSCT outright, so the mechanism travels and her eligibility does not.

Araki's finding that MRD-positive morphologic CR behaved like active disease at transplant (3-year relapse 67% versus 65%) cuts both ways here: it weakens the case for spending toxicity on a shallow remission first, and it is drawn from first transplants.

notes: A few things I want on the record before round 2. First, the source case's preferences.json carries an empty toxicity_vetoes list, so I am not enforcing a stated veto against anyone in round 1. What I am enforcing is a threshold: no baseline creatinine clearance, no LFTs, no cardiac assessment exists anywhere in this case, and every intensive candidate on this board assumes organ function that has never been measured. Any rank-1 pick that puts mitoxantrone, daunorubicin or high-dose cytarabine into her without that documentation is a veto candidate in round 2, and the veto lifts the moment the labs land in normal range. Second, on the shape of the question. It asks what maximises CR probability, not what is safest, and I have tried not to answer a different question. But the CR-maximising framing hides a denominator problem the board should see plainly: Giles puts second-salvage true CR at 13% of 594 and 0% in his highest-risk group, MIRROS's randomised control arm managed 17.1% true CR, and post-venetoclax salvage produced 23% ORR in 22 patients. A regimen offering a 15% to 25% chance of the intended result with a 7% to 21% chance of killing her inside 60 days is a different proposition from the 58% headline, and the 58% comes from a population that contains none of her hard features. Third, and this one is not hedging: no candidate here has CR data in which anyone looked at an extramedullary lesion, apart from two paediatric patients imaged on gemtuzumab. Any CR claim this board makes is a marrow claim and should be written as one.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF, fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
picks.rationale: This is the one open protocol whose eligibility was written to admit her: post-allo relapse at 60 days or more, GVHD no worse than grade 1, no blast or WBC cap, and prior fludarabine not an exclusion. It clears the two preferences she did state that bear on this decision, that trials are acceptable including travel and that no modality is ruled out. What it cannot give her is a number: NCT04050280 has posted nothing in refractory AML and the only CLAG-GO publication is frontline core-binding-factor disease, so ranking it first rests on eligibility and on the backbone, not on a CR rate for this combination. Her nearest honest anchors run from 13% (second-salvage true CR, n=594) through 26% (fractionated gemtuzumab monotherapy in first relapse, an upper bound) to 58% (CLAG-M true CR, pre-venetoclax, no post-allo subgroup), and she should be told the spread is that wide.
primary_concerns: Two gates are unverified in her chart and either one closes this door: CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, which she has only as qualitative flow, and creatinine below 1.8 mg/dL with direct bilirubin under twice normal, which is undocumented organ function.
The protocol says nothing about assessing the thigh lesion at response. A CR from it would be a marrow CR, and calling it anything else would be telling her she got a result she did not get.

Preference conflict, stated rather than resolved: her efficacy weight of 0.75 was set before fitness was known and preferences.json asks for it to be revisited. ECOG 1 is now on the record; cardiac and organ function are not, so half that condition is still open and this pick is conditional on closing it.

The only source anywhere in the file that measured an extramedullary CD33-positive lesion at response is two paediatric patients on serial FDG-PET/CT. That is a method worth copying, not an estimate for her thigh.

picks.intervention_label: Sequential (FLAMSA-type) conditioning into a second allograft; US platforms NCT06928662 and NCT04375631
picks.rationale: ASAP is the only randomised test of whether inducing CR before a graft is worth doing, and day-56 post-transplant CR came out at 83% with disease control against 79% with HAM induction, at 27 fewer hospital days; non-inferiority was not formally shown (p=0.036) and prior allograft was an exclusion, so the trial cannot be read onto her. It still puts the question nobody has asked her in front of the board: whether the remission she wants is one the conditioning produces, rather than one she has to buy first with a separate reinduction. She has an HLA-identical CMV-negative sibling, curative intent on the record, and no modality ruled out, and both US platforms admit her on paper, with prior TBI up to 3 Gy permitted beyond six months, no blast cap, and refractoriness to FLAG-Ida not itself an exclusion. FLAMSA's 88% true CR came from mostly first transplants two decades before venetoclax-era salvage, so it argues mechanism and not her rate.
primary_concerns: Two of the three entry gates are undocumented and both are hard: creatinine clearance above 60 mL/min and DLCO at or above 70%. ECOG 1 is the only one she has already met.
Neither open platform reports a remission endpoint, so choosing this route means accepting that no CR figure will ever attach to it. On the question as literally asked, that is a real cost.
Durability and sequencing are out of scope here by design, and durability is where a second graft's case actually lives. She cannot act on this rank without the source dossier open beside it.
SIERRA showed radioimmunoconditioning can carry active disease to a durable CR at 17.1% versus 0%, and it excluded prior HCT, as does its successor. The mechanism is validated and the door is shut.

picks.intervention_label: Hypomethylating agent plus venetoclax (off-protocol, deliverable now)
picks.rationale: Closest published population to hers on the axis that bears hardest: 83 patients relapsing after an allograft, 55% with prior venetoclax and 28% of those already venetoclax-failed, and prior venetoclax failure did not predict worse survival. Thirty-day mortality was 3.6%, and this is the option that survives a poor fitness read, which matters precisely because the fitness assessment her own preference file asks for has not happened. The 48% is CR or CRi pooled with no CR-only split, so it is not a CR rate and must not be set beside 13% or 17.1% as though it were. Median time to relapse in that cohort was 7 months against her six years, response was assessed on marrow with no extramedullary reporting, and a lower-intensity regimen against roughly 85% marrow blasts is a different proposition from the low-burden disease most of those patients carried.
primary_concerns: She is refractory to FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax. BAX loss in 17% of post-venetoclax relapses and a global fall in apoptotic priming both say cross-resistance is variable rather than absent, which cuts against a venetoclax-containing answer without settling it.
The pessimistic anchor on her own axis is 23% response after venetoclax-salvage failure in 28 heavily pretreated patients, and even that pools CR with morphological leukaemia-free state.
Preference silence, flagged not assumed: nothing she has said tells us she would trade CR probability for a lower-intensity course with fewer hospital days. That trade was never put to her.

picks.intervention_label: CPX-351 plus venetoclax, NCT03629171
picks.rationale: The only deliverable option with published results in a cohort resembling her prior-therapy history: 58% had prior venetoclax, 30% a prior transplant, 44% were in second salvage or later. Read precisely, true CR was 15% and the composite CRc 39%; the 70% CRc belongs to first-salvage TP53-wild-type patients and she is in neither group. Prior anthracycline exposure and her unresolved TP53 both cut against her landing where the regimen performed. It is recruiting, which clears her trials preference, and the 15% is the most honest figure in this file about what a venetoclax-containing salvage does once venetoclax has already failed.
primary_concerns: A 15% true CR is roughly a one-in-seven chance of the result she is picturing when she hears complete remission, before the thigh lesion is even counted. Whether that trade is worth taking is a question for her, and nobody has put it to her.
Single centre, n=33, and the file publishes no confidence interval around the 15%.
The 39% composite is the number that will get quoted if anyone is careless, and it is not what she asked about.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-M off protocol (fallback if the CLAG-GO gates fail)
picks.rationale: The fallback that keeps her from being stranded if CD33 quantification or bilirubin closes NCT04050280: every drug is on the shelf, and the 58% is a true CR in 118 poor-risk refractory or relapsed patients, the largest true-CR denominator here. That 58% is not her number and should never be handed to her as one, since the study closed before venetoclax existed and reports no post-allo subgroup, and Giles resets the frame to 13% once a patient reaches second salvage. Her long first remission counts in her favour on that risk model, while roughly 85% marrow blasts and non-inv(16) disease count against. The single retrospective head-to-head in the file favours a cladribine backbone over MEC on true CR (37.9% versus 23.8%), and MEC's own blast-burden gradient argues against MEC at her load.
primary_concerns: Off-protocol intensive salvage carrying substantial treatment-related mortality, in a patient whose organ function is undocumented, is the exact combination her preference file flagged as unresolved and asked to have revisited.
WBC above 10 g/L predicted failure in the CLAG-M cohort; her peripheral blasts ran 58 to 82% across late June 2026.
Off protocol also means no trial infrastructure and no protocol-mandated response assessment, so the extramedullary question would have to be built in deliberately.

notes: FRAMING AUDIT (asked of me, answered plainly). The question that got researched is the question she asked. I checked all four narrowings for the failure mode where a hard question is quietly swapped for an easier neighbour, and three of them move the other way. Widening 'therapy' past profiled features was necessary, not permissive: a targetable_features read would have deleted CLAG-M, MEC, HMA-VEN and every conditioning platform, which is most of what she can actually be given. Pinning 'complete remission' to ELN 2022, with composites labelled and marrow CR alongside a persistent sarcoma reported as exactly that, makes the question harder to answer, not easier, and it is the single narrowing that most protects her. Pinning 'at this point' to next line with the workup concurrent matches the decision her team faces within weeks. The fourth narrowing is the one to keep an eye on. 'Most likely' as she asked it is a question about her odds; the framer converted it to best-evidenced likelihood in matched populations, which is a published cohort's rate, and for her there is no matched cohort. That conversion is legitimate and the framer stated its limits, but it permits rather than forces the honest answer, which is that nobody can quote her a personal number. My residual worry is not the framing, it is the reading: a page headed 'most likely to induce a complete remission' with a ranked list under it will be read as 'what to do', which the out_of_scope list explicitly forbids. The guard was written; the board has to hold it. One gap I would name as hers: nothing in the scope spine measures what a treatment costs her in weeks of her life. ASAP's 27 hospital days appears in the file as evidence, never as an endpoint. PREFERENCE AUDIT (the unusual part). preferences.json belongs to the source case, and its free text says the EXPLICIT reason for that run was HLA-restricted immunotherapy eligibility, which this question puts out of scope. The file was aimed elsewhere. What it supports here: prefers_trials true and trials acceptable INCLUDING travel, fully satisfied by ranks 1, 2 and 4; modality_constraints empty and no modality ruled out, genuinely clear, so intensive inpatient salvage is not blocked by anything she said; curative intent on the record, which is why rank 2 belongs in this list at all. What it does not support: efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.75 cannot be leaned on, because the file itself asks for it to be revisited once fitness is known and organ function is still undocumented (ECOG 1 has since been recorded, so half the condition is met). And toxicity_vetoes is an empty array, which is not permission. An empty veto list means nobody has offered her a 13 to 17% chance of the intended result against substantial treatment-related mortality and asked whether she wants it. Any persona reading the empty array as consent to maximise CR at any cost is importing a preference she never expressed. Four axes are silent and each is decision-relevant, so I am naming them rather than filling them in: how much CR probability she would trade for how much toxicity; whether a marrow CR with the thigh lesion still there counts as the result she means; how she weighs hospital days against remission odds; and whether she would accept going straight to conditioning without a CR first. WHAT MUST REACH HER. Every CR figure in this file is marrow-only. Molecular profiles diverged between sarcoma and marrow in 56% of paired samples, and 46% of post-transplant relapses were isolated extramedullary, so a marrow CR cannot be assumed to cover her thigh. The best-matched signal in the dossier is not deliverable: lintuzumab-Ac225 plus CLAG-M carried 50% in TP53-mutated and 38.5% in prior-venetoclax patients, all composite CR/CRi with single-digit denominators, and the trial completed with its follow-on suspended. The best-fitting open protocol has zero published results. Both facts are hers, not the board's.

picks.intervention_label: CPX-351 (liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine) plus venetoclax (NCT03629171)
picks.rationale: Kadia's protocol is the only prospective study in this file that enrolled her kind of patient and still published a true CR apart from the composite: 15% CR (5/33) against 39% CRc, in a cohort where 58% had prior venetoclax, 30% had a prior transplant and 44% were at second salvage or later. Her stratum inside that protocol reads 26% CRc (6/23), not the 70% (n=10) quoted for first-salvage TP53-wild-type patients, and 26% sits on top of Giles' 13% second-salvage true CR (76/594) rather than above it. I rank it first because its number is the most transferable one available, not because it is the largest number in the file. Single-arm, single-institution, n=33, marrow-only response assessment, 60-day mortality 21%.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I confounding and selection: no comparator arm, treatment assignment is enrolment onto an open protocol at one institution, and nothing in the analysis adjusts for who got offered it.
Power. The Wilson interval on 5/33 runs 6.7 to 30.9, which contains the Giles 13% floor and the MEC 33.3% true CR alike. It cannot rule either in or out.
The 70% versus 26% CRc split is within-protocol and one response definition, which is worth something, but it is unadjusted, was not the registered primary endpoint, and the 26% arm has 23 patients.

Every efficacy figure is marrow. Padmanabhan found discordant mutation profiles between myeloid sarcoma tissue and marrow in 56% of 112 paired samples, so a marrow CR here does not license a claim about the thigh.

Preclinically the direction is unhelpful: blasts from patients who went on to achieve CR were more sensitive to CPX-351 than blasts from chemotherapy-refractory patients, and against CD34+CD38- blasts the liposome was no better than free drug at the same ratio. The formulation buys therapeutic index, not potency against a refractory clone.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-M (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, mitoxantrone, G-CSF), off-protocol
picks.rationale: This is one of the few true CR rates in the dossier attached to a deliverable intensive backbone, and at 118 patients across 11 Polish centres it is the largest of them. It is also not her rate: the study closed before venetoclax existed and reports no post-allograft subgroup, and the printed 58% does not reconcile with the stated 66/118, which is 55.9%; 58% matches the 114 evaluable denominator. Price's CLAG versus MEC comparison (37.9% vs 23.8% true CR, p=0.048, n=162) is the only head-to-head in the file, and it is a single-centre chart review with treatment assigned by physician choice and no adjustment reported. Recalibrated through Giles, I would expect this backbone to land somewhere in the teens to twenties in her position rather than the high fifties.
primary_concerns: Indirectness is the load-bearing flaw, not bias: neither the 2008 phase 2 nor the 2011 comparison contains a single post-allo-HCT relapse or a venetoclax-refractory patient, and no matched CLAG-M series exists to fall back on.
Wierzbowska scored CR by the era's morphologic criteria, which is not the ELN 2022 bar this question set.
ROBINS-I for Price 2011: confounding by indication, no adjustment, single centre, retrospective, and p=0.048 on an unadjusted comparison is not a result I would rank a patient's therapy on.
Blast burden points the wrong way. Zhong's MEC cohort found marrow blasts at or below 20% and peripheral blasts at or below 30% more than doubled the odds of CR/CRi; she is at roughly 85% and 82%.
Organ function is undocumented and she has already had FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax. The 7% early-death figure (8/118) comes from a fitter, mostly first-salvage cohort.

picks.intervention_label: Hypomethylating agent plus venetoclax in post-allograft relapse
picks.rationale: Samuels is the closest published population to hers on the axis that matters most, 83 patients relapsing after allograft with 55% prior venetoclax exposure, and it is the only source here that tested prior venetoclax failure against outcome and found it did not predict worse survival. What it cannot supply is a CR rate: 48% is CR or CRi pooled across 40/83 with no split published, and the paper reported MLFS separately (2/83), so the pooling was a choice rather than a constraint. Pooling matters more for her than for most, because a marrow conditioned once already recovers counts slowly, which is the difference between CR and CRi. Byrne's post-allograft venetoclax series does split it, and there the true CR was 5 of 19, not the 42.1% composite.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I: retrospective single-centre cohort, confounding by indication, selection of who was well enough to be treated, and no protocol-defined response timepoint.

Endpoint. The composite is the only figure published, so a CR-only estimate for this regimen in her population does not exist. Fleischmann's post-allograft 42.8% is worse still, pooling complete with partial remission.

Population match breaks on burden and timing: median relapse was 7.0 months post-HCT and marrow burden is not reported. She relapsed at about six years with roughly 85% marrow and 82% peripheral blasts, where a low-intensity regimen is an extrapolation rather than an application.
She is already venetoclax-refractory. Zucenka's post-venetoclax salvage cohort is the closer anchor, and its 23% pools CR with morphologic leukaemia-free state across 22 patients.

picks.intervention_label: Venetoclax plus high-dose cytarabine and mitoxantrone (RELAX, NCT04330820)
picks.rationale: 75% is the largest remission figure among the deliverable backbones and it is a composite CRc, 41/55 by ITT, with no CR-only split published in the abstract, in the PMC record, or on NCT04330820, which carries hasResults=false. It has the largest post-transplant fraction of any prospective salvage cohort here, 19 of 55 (35%), which is the reason it stays on my list at all. The abstract's own safety line does not reconcile: 15 serious adverse events in 14 (13%) patients, when 14 of 55 is 25%. Until a CR-only number exists, setting 75% beside CLAG-M's 58% or MEC's 33.3% compares two different endpoints, and I would object to it being quoted that way in a treatment discussion.
primary_concerns: Selective outcome reporting under RoB 2: the composite is published and its components are not, in a trial whose registry entry posts no results.

An unresolved internal inconsistency in the reported denominator for serious adverse events, in the only source available. I have read the abstract and the PMC commentary, not the full text, so I cannot say which figure is wrong.
Single-arm phase 1/2 with no comparator, so the composite carries all the usual selection and confounding of an enrolled cohort.
Deliverability is not established either: the registry record's recruitment status reads unknown, and an unknown-status European protocol is not a route to therapy within weeks.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (CLAG plus fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
picks.rationale: I rank this as an access route, not as evidence, and the distinction should survive into the write-up. NCT04050280 is written to admit her post-allograft relapse with no blast or WBC cap, and it has published nothing in refractory AML; the one CLAG-GO efficacy paper found is frontline core-binding-factor AML, a favourable-risk treatment-naive population with no overlap with her disease or line. The 56.6% composite that travels with this regimen in conversation belongs to CLAG-M plus lintuzumab-Ac225, 26 patients, composite CR/CRi, no CR split, and its 50% TP53 and 38.5% prior-venetoclax subgroups have single-digit denominators. Fractionated gemtuzumab's own clean figure is 26% CR (15/57) in first relapse, transplant-naive and venetoclax-naive, which is a ceiling for her rather than an estimate.
primary_concerns: No published efficacy in the indication at all. Any CR probability attached to this arm is borrowed from a different regimen, and the borrowing should be named wherever the rank appears.

Attribution error is the specific risk: the 56.6% is lintuzumab-Ac225 plus CLAG-M from a phase 1 dose-escalation whose follow-on NCT06802523 is suspended, so it is neither this regimen's number nor a deliverable one.

CD33 is positive by qualitative flow only with density unquantified, and MyloFrance-1 tracked P-glycoprotein and MRP1 efflux rather than CD33 density, so there is no published dose-response on the axis that would justify the ADC choice.

The only extramedullary CD33 response data anywhere in the file are two paediatric patients followed by serial FDG-PET/CT with neither response graded as CR. That is a method worth copying and not a rate.

notes: How I read the seven pre-registered criteria. (1) Not found. No prospective trial or multicentre cohort of 20 or more reports a true CR rate in a post-allograft or post-venetoclax-failure population that is clearly higher than the alternatives; the one prospective true-CR figure from a matched cohort is CPX-351 plus venetoclax at 15% (5/33), which is below the unmatched competitors rather than above them. (2) Not found as pre-registered, which required applicability after a prior allograft. FLAMSA's 88% CR (66/75) is overwhelmingly first transplants and predates venetoclax-era salvage, SIERRA excluded prior HCT outright, NCT05807932 excludes anyone treated beyond hydroxyurea or two HMA courses, and NCT06928662 and NCT04375631 will take her but have published no remission data. (3) Lands for CLAG-M and for CLAG-GO. It does not land for CPX-351 plus venetoclax, which is the reason that pick is rank 1 despite the smallest headline. (4) Lands, and this is the finding I would put in front of the synthesist. On true CR in populations that contain her, the Wilson intervals are CPX-351 plus venetoclax 6.7 to 30.9 (5/33), Byrne post-allograft venetoclax 11.8 to 48.8 (5/19), the MIRROS control arm 11.4 to 24.7 (21/123) and Giles second salvage 10.3 to 15.7 (76/594). Every one of those overlaps every other one. The intervals that do clear the pack belong either to composite endpoints (RELAX CRc 61.7 to 84.2) or to populations she is not in (CLAG-M 46.9 to 64.6), and both separations are artefacts of the comparison rather than findings about her. If the answer shape stays verdict_plus_ranked_options, the ranking has to be labelled as ordering by evidence quality and population match, because it is not ordering by demonstrated CR probability. (5) Technically met, practically not. McNeil measured two paediatric extramedullary lesions by serial FDG-PET/CT with no CR grading, Shatilova is one patient, and Lazzarotto's 45% (19/43) does not state whether extramedullary sites were assessed at response. Every CR claim in the final answer needs the marrow-only caveat. (6) Lands. Lintuzumab-Ac225 plus CLAG-M has the best subgroup numbers on two of her three hardest axes and the trial is completed with NCT06802523 suspended; flotetuzumab's 47% in TP53-abnormal disease is 7/15, post-hoc, defined as under 5% marrow blasts without count recovery rather than ELN CR, on a terminated programme; uproleselan reports CR separately (35%, 19/54) and its confirmatory phase 3 in R/R AML terminated. (7) Met only by Price 2011, at a grade too weak to rank on. Two further items for the record. Alwash found a newly detectable TP53 mutation in 36% of post-transplant patients who were wild-type at diagnosis, so her negative 2026 panel at a 2% limit of detection with no CNV coverage is not reassurance in either direction, and that paper's burden split (composite CR/CRi 41% below 20% VAF against 13% at or above) is the figure that would move if the variant resolves. And the Wierzbowska row prints 58% alongside a stated 66/118, which is 55.9%; 58% is 66 of the 114 evaluable. Minor, but that is how a number drifts once it starts being quoted.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO on protocol (NCT04050280)
picks.rationale: NCCN AML routes relapsed/refractory disease to a clinical trial or to the salvage regimens used for R/R disease, wording the guideline has carried since at least v3.2019, and the panel's standing line is that the best management of any patient with cancer is in a clinical trial. The guideline is now at v3.2026, and no version has promoted a named regimen to a second-salvage endorsement in a post-allograft patient, so the trial route is the endorsement here rather than a fallback. NCT04050280 is the only open protocol whose eligibility text was written to admit her: post-allo relapse eligible from day 60, no blast or WBC cap, prior fludarabine not excluded. The endorsement covers the route, not the regimen. CLAG-GO has published no CR rate in refractory AML at all.
primary_concerns: Protocol gate she has not cleared: CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, and her flow is qualitative only. Creatinine under 1.8 mg/dL and direct bilirubin under twice normal are also undocumented.
No NCCN category and no ELN recommendation attaches to CLAG-GO itself. Trial-preferred routing tells you how to be treated, not what CR rate to expect.
Given off protocol, CLAG-GO is an off-label combination. Only the gemtuzumab component carries an indication for this line.
The protocol excludes isolated myeloid sarcoma but says nothing about assessing her thigh lesion at response, so a CR on this study would be a marrow CR.

picks.intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy
picks.rationale: This is the only candidate in the file whose label matches her line: FDA-approved for relapsed or refractory CD33-positive AML at 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7, which is the MyloFrance-1 schedule that gave 26% true CR in 57 patients. Those 57 were in first relapse, transplant-naive and venetoclax-naive, so 26% is a ceiling she sits under rather than an estimate for her. It is also the only source in the dossier where anyone imaged a CD33-positive extramedullary lesion at response, and that was two children. I rank it second because label carriage is the closest thing to an endorsement that survives contact with her actual line of therapy.
primary_concerns: Boxed warning for hepatotoxicity including fatal veno-occlusive disease, which weighs more in a woman with a prior allograft who may be heading toward a second one.
26% CR comes from a population that excludes her on all three of her hard axes at once.

A label is not an NCCN category. NCCN's default is that all recommendations are category 2A unless otherwise noted, and I could not open the v3.2026 PDF to confirm what the panel attaches to gemtuzumab in second salvage, so I am naming no category for it.

picks.intervention_label: Sequential conditioning into second allogeneic HCT (NCT06928662, or NCT04375631 with a cladribine backbone)
picks.rationale: The guidelines answer a question this board has not asked out loud: nothing in them conditions a second allograft on achieving CR first. ELN 2022 handles post-transplant relapse through second HCT and DLI without writing a remission precondition into either, and the one randomised test of inducing CR before transplant, ASAP, read day-56 post-transplant CR of 83% with watchful waiting against 79% with HAM induction (ITT difference 3.4%, 95% CI -5.8 to 12.6). Non-inferiority was not shown at the pre-specified 2.5% level (p=0.036) and induction was not better either, while induction cost 61% versus 21% grade 3 or worse non-haematological adverse events and a median 27 extra hospital days. ASAP enrolled patients heading to a first allograft, so it does not transfer to her, and no guideline has absorbed it: ELN 2022 predates it and the v3.2026 NCCN Insights were about MRD.
primary_concerns: Guideline silence on a CR precondition is not an endorsement of transplanting at 85% blasts. It licenses the conversation, not the decision.
Both protocols have mortality and disease-free survival as primary endpoints, so neither will produce a CR rate to set against reinduction.
Three undocumented gates, each hard: ECOG 0-1, creatinine clearance above 60 mL/min, DLCO at or above 70%.
The 88% CR from FLAMSA sequential conditioning came from mostly first transplants two decades before venetoclax. It is not a number she can be quoted.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-M off protocol (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, mitoxantrone, G-CSF)
picks.rationale: If no protocol slot opens, cladribine and high-dose-cytarabine aggressive salvage is the class NCCN carries for R/R AML, and the panel's own default is that all recommendations are category 2A unless otherwise noted, which means uniform consensus on lower-level evidence rather than trial-grade proof. The Polish multicentre series gave 58% true CR (66 of 118), one of the few CR-only figures anywhere in this dossier, but it closed before venetoclax existed and reports no post-allograft subgroup. Second salvage recalibrates that hard: 13% true CR across 594 patients, and no patient in the highest-risk group remitted at all. I would not quote 58% to this woman.
primary_concerns: Guideline carriage of the class does not carry the number. No NCCN category attaches to a CR rate in second salvage after intensive chemotherapy plus venetoclax has failed.
The guideline population is fit patients with documented organ function. Hers is undocumented, and that is the gate on any intensive salvage.
Marrow-only response assessment. ELN 2022 CR requires absence of extramedullary disease, and no salvage series here imaged one.

picks.intervention_label: Hypomethylating agent plus venetoclax for post-allograft relapse
picks.rationale: The closest published population to hers on the transplant axis: 83 patients relapsing after allograft, 48% composite CR/CRi with no CR-only split, and the only series in the file where prior venetoclax failure was tested against outcome and did not predict it. On guideline fit it is the weakest thing on my list. Venetoclax is labelled for newly diagnosed AML in adults unfit for intensive induction and NCCN carries the doublet in that frontline slot, so post-allograft salvage after venetoclax failure is off-label on indication and on line. She is already refractory to venetoclax, and no amount of guideline silence covers that.
primary_concerns: Off-label on indication, on line, and on prior-exposure status.
48% is composite CR/CRi and the paper publishes no CR-only split, so it cannot be reported as a CR rate under this question's rules.
Marrow-only assessment again, and the pessimistic anchor for her exact axis is 23% response after venetoclax salvage failure, a figure that itself pools CR with MLFS.

notes: Four guideline findings for the record. (1) CPX-351 carriage is frontline only. Vyxeos is labelled for newly diagnosed t-AML or AML-MRC (label effective 2026-01-30), and NCCN's carriage sits in that slot, where v3.2019 gave it category 2B for the under-60 group because the pivotal trial had not included them. CPX-351 plus venetoclax in second salvage is off-indication as well as off-label, whatever the phase 2 reads. (2) ELN 2022 CR requires absence of extramedullary disease as part of the definition, but names no modality and no timing for assessing it. That does not license marrow-only CR claims in a woman with a documented thigh sarcoma. It means the CR figures in this file, all of them marrow-only, are not ELN CRs for a patient like her, and the thigh needs imaging at response if the team wants a defensible call. (3) Staleness. NCCN AML is at v3.2026, Insights published June 2026 and scoped to MRD monitoring and management; ELN 2022 is four years old and predates ASAP, RELAX and the post-allograft HMA-venetoclax series. The EBMT DLI best-practice recommendations (Lancet Haematol 2024) are consensus built mostly on retrospective data, which is worth knowing before anyone leans on DLI guidance for a patient at 85% blasts. (4) I could not open the v3.2026 PDF, which sits behind an NCCN login, so I have named no per-regimen category I could not verify from an accessible source. Guideline silence on second salvage after intensive chemotherapy plus venetoclax in a post-allograft patient is not a hidden endorsement of anything. It is the consensus saying this patient belongs on a protocol.
